summary: The Helping Optimize Prevention and Engagement for Heroes Act of 2025, or HOPE for Heroes Act of 2025, amends the Commander John Scott Hannon Veterans Mental Health Care Improvement Act of 2019. It modifies and reauthorizes the Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program through September 30, 2030. The bill changes grant amounts, adds performance-based bonus amounts, introduces limits on administrative and food/beverage costs, mandates specific screening tools like the Columbia Protocol, adds transportation services, and adjusts rules regarding emergent suicide care and coordination between the Department of Veterans Affairs and local grant recipients.

affected_groups.effect: They face new funding caps, mandatory screening protocols such as the Columbia Protocol, coordination requirements with local VA medical centers, and are eligible for higher maximum and performance-based grant amounts.

They gain access to transportation or rideshare services for appointments, standardized suicide severity screening, and automatic eligibility for emergent suicide care if VA mental health care services are not provided within 72 hours of a referral.
affected_groups.group: Veterans and eligible individuals seeking suicide prevention services

affected_groups.effect: Department officials must provide additional training to employees on the grant program, conduct quarterly briefings for local medical centers, and oversee new performance metrics and compliance reporting.
affected_groups.group: Department of Veterans Affairs and its employees

key_provisions: Increases the maximum standard grant amount from $750,000 to $1,000,000 and allows performance-based additional amounts up to $500,000 per grantee per fiscal year.
Limits grant fund usage so that not more than 30 percent may be spent on administrative costs and not more than five percent on food and beverages.
Extends the duration and reauthorization of the grant program through September 30, 2030.
Requires grant recipients to use the Columbia Protocol (Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale) for screening and to coordinate communication plans with local suicide prevention coordinators.
Adds transportation and rideshare services for eligible individuals to use for appointments as a permitted suicide prevention service.

Provides that if the Secretary does not provide mental health or behavioral health care services within the 72-hour period following a referral, the individual shall be treated as eligible for emergent suicide care.
Requires quarterly briefings for local Department of Veterans Affairs medical centers located within 100 miles of a grant recipient to improve coordination.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Helping Optimize Prevention and Engagement for Heroes Act of 2025, or HOPE for Heroes Act of 2025, amends the Commander John Scott Hannon Veterans Mental Health Care Improvement Act of 2019. It modifies and reauthorizes the Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program through September 30, 2030. The bill changes grant amounts, adds performance-based bonus amounts, introduces limits on administrative and food/beverage costs, mandates specific screening tools like the Columbia Protocol, adds transportation services, and adjusts rules regarding emergent suicide care and coordination between the Department of Veterans Affairs and local grant recipients.
summary_detail.significance: The bill modifies and extends the Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program until 2030, alters funding caps and structures, adds transportation options for appointments, and refines administrative and clinical coordination between community grant recipients and Department of Veterans Affairs medical facilities. Measured against total federal operations, its impact is limited to veteran mental health grants and specialized suicide prevention services.
